verses.zh: 凡在轭下作仆人的，当以自己主人配受十分的恭敬，免得　神的名和道理被人亵渎。
verses.en: Those who are under the yoke as slaves[NOTE:1] must regard their own masters as deserving of full respect. This will prevent[NOTE:2] the name of God and Christian teaching[NOTE:3] from being discredited.[NOTE:4]
notes: Traditionally, “servants.” Though δοῦλος (doulos) is normally translated “servant,” the word does not bear the connotation of a free individual serving another. BDAG notes that “‘servant’ for ‘slave’ is largely confined to Biblical transl. and early American times…in normal usage at the present time the two words are carefully distinguished” (BDAG 260 s.v.). One good translation is “bondservant” (sometimes found in the ASV for δοῦλος) in that it often indicates one who sells himself into slavery to another. But as this is archaic, few today understand its force. Also, many slaves in the Roman world became slaves through Rome’s subjugation of conquered nations, kidnapping, or by being born into slave households.
Grk “that the name…may not be slandered” (a continuation of the preceding sentence).
Grk “the teaching.”
Or “slandered.”
verses.commentary:
6:1 "All who are under the yoke as slaves" Christianity adapted itself to the culture of
its day in regards to slavery. Two-thirds of the Roman world were slaves. It was the truth, justice,
and love of God in the gospel that eventually brought slavery to an end. Paul chose to deal with
human attitudes in their cultural situation instead of a violent overthrow of that cultural situation
(much like he did the societal role of women; see Gordon Fee, The Gospel and Spirit).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S ADMONITIONS TO SLAVES

▣ "to regard their own masters as worthy of all honor" Apparently verse 1 refers
to Christian slaves serving non-Christian masters (cf. Eph. 6:5-8), while verse 2 refers to Christian slaves
serving Christian masters (cf. Eph. 6:9). A Christian slave is to act toward believers and unbelievers in such
a way as to bring honor to God and the gospel of Jesus Christ (cf. Eph. 6:6-7). Verse 1 has the
same orientation as 1 Tim. 3:2,7,10; 5:7,8,14; and Titus 2:5, which means "no handle for criticism."
Also see 1 Tim. 6:14 of this same chapter.

verses.zh: 仆人有信道的主人，不可因为与他是弟兄就轻看他；更要加意服事他；因为得服事之益处的，是信道蒙爱的。你要以此教训人，劝勉人。
verses.en: But those who have believing masters must not show them less respect[NOTE:1] because they are brothers. Instead they are to serve all the more, because those who benefit from their service are believers and dearly loved.[NOTE:2] Teach them and exhort them about these things.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “think the less of them”; Grk “despise them,” “look down on them.”
Or “those who devote themselves to service are faithful and dearly loved” (referring to slaves who serve them).
Grk “these things teach and exhort.”
verses.commentary:
6:2 "Those who have believers as their masters must not be disrespectful to them" This is
literally "look down,"which is a PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE with the
NEGATIVE PARTICLE, implying stop an act already in process. This phrase relates
to the doctrinal concept that everything we as believers do must be of the highest quality for
Christ's sake (cf. 1 Cor. 10:31; Eph. 6:6-7; Col. 3:17; 1 Pet. 4:11; also note the NT book of Philemon).

The term "masters" is not the normal term for slave owner, kurios
(cf. Eph. 6:5,9; Col. 3:22; 4:1), but despotēs. It is usually used of God the Father and
the Son, but in the Pastoral Letters it is used regularly for earthly slave masters (cf. 1 Tim. 6:1,2;
2 Tim. 2:21; Titus 2:9). Paul may have used a different scribe.

▣ "Teach and preach these principles" These are two
PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVES, which implies a continual obligation (cf. 1 Tim. 4:11).
This phrase can conclude the previous admonition (cf. NASB, NKJV) or introduce what follows
(cf. NRSV, TEV, NJB). Remember, chapter and verse divisions are not inspired.

verses.zh: 若有人传异教，不服从我们主耶稣基督纯正的话与那合乎敬虔的道理，
verses.en: If someone spreads false teachings[NOTE:1] and does not agree with sound words (that is, those of our Lord Jesus Christ) and with the teaching that accords with godliness,
notes: Grk “teaches other doctrines,” (different from apostolic teaching, cf. 1 Tim 1:3).
verses.commentary:
6:3 "If" This is a FIRST CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE (which is assumed
to be true) continuing the literary context from 1 Tim. 6:3 through 1 Tim. 6:5. There were false teachers
who rejected Paul's teachings (cf. 1 Tim. 1:3-7; 4:1-3). They were in the churches (cf. 1 John 2:18-19).

▣ "advocates a different doctrine" This is the Greek term heteros, which
means "another of a different kind." The false teaching was a combination of Jewish legalism
and Greek philosophy similar to that found in Colossians and Ephesians.

▣ "and does not agree with sound words" See note at 1 Tim. 1:10.

▣ "those of our Lord Jesus Christ" Paul asserts that the origin of the "sound words"
is Christ's teachings which were given to Paul. These false teachers rejected both Christ and His
Apostles' teachings.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRIST JESUS AS LORD

▣ "and with doctrine conforming to godliness" See note at 1 Tim. 2:2. Christ's
teachings always had godliness as their goal (cf. 1 Tim. 3:16). These false teachers tried to
separate truth from life, justification from sanctification, the INDICATIVE (gospel truth)
from the IMPERATIVE (gospel godliness). Eternal life has observable characteristics (cf. Matt. 7:15-23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GODLINESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEW TESTAMENT HOLINESS/SANCTIFICATION

verses.zh: 他是自高自大，一无所知，专好问难，争辩言词，从此就生出嫉妒、纷争、毁谤、妄疑，
verses.en: he is conceited and understands nothing, but has an unhealthy interest in controversies and verbal disputes. This gives rise to envy, dissension, slanders, evil suspicions,
verses.commentary:
6:4

NASB, NRSV
"he is conceited"

NKJV, NJB, Peshitta
"he is proud"

TEV
"is swollen with pride"

This is a PERFECT PASSIVE INDICATIVE. The term is literally
"smoke-blinded" by means of pride (cf. 1 Tim. 3:6; 6:4; 2 Tim. 3:4). This is not ignorance but self-willed blindness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: VICES AND VIRTUES IN THE NT

▣ "but he has a morbid interest in controversial questions and disputes about words" There
has been an ongoing emphasis on Timothy not being involved in these futile discussions of the false
teachers (cf. 1 Tim. 1:3,4; 4:7; 2 Tim. 2:14; 4:4; Titus 1:14). I wonder how this would apply today?

The term "morbid" is literally "to be sick." It came to be used as imagery for an
intense craving for something. These false teachers were not seeking godliness, but wanting esoteric
knowledge about unrevealed areas or peripheral areas of truth. They wanted to argue over oblique
doctrinal issues which only caused arguments and prideful divisions.

The older I get the more I know I do not know and the happier I am with less
understanding! The main truths of Christianity are clear and repeated! Yet, somehow we strive
to know "all" the details and implications and weave theological webs containing all the inferences
of difficult, oblique, apocalyptic and prophetic passages. We glory in our detailed systems instead
of our relationship with Christ. It may be harder for a dogmatic, systematic theologian to go through
the eye of a needle than for a rich person!!

Preach the clear truths! Discuss the peripherals in love! Be gracious to all!
Maturity will make us less judgmental and more Christlike.

verses.zh: 并那坏了心术、失丧真理之人的争竞。他们以敬虔为得利的门路。
verses.en: and constant bickering by people corrupted in their minds and deprived of the truth, who suppose that godliness[NOTE:1] is a way of making a profit.
notes: Although most witnesses, including some early versions and fathers (D2 Ψ 1241 1505 M al sy Cyp Lcf Ambst), have ἀφίστασο ἀπὸ τῶν τοιούτων (aphistaso apo’ tōn toioutōn, “stay away from such things!”) after εὐσεβείαν (eusebeian, “godliness”; thus, “who suppose that godliness is a way of making a profit; stay away from such things!”), there seems to be little reason for this clause’s omission in some of the oldest and best witnesses (א A D* F G 048 6 33 81 1175 1739 1881 lat co). It is likely that it crept into the text early, perhaps as a marginal comment, but it should not be considered authentic in light of the strong external and transcriptional evidence against it.
verses.commentary:
6:5 "men of depraved mind" This refers to either

- the entire context refers to the false teachers

- the first few verses refer to them and the rest refers to the consequences
caused in the local house churches by their teachings (cf. Arichea and Hatton's
A Handbook on Paul's Letters to Timothy and Titus, UBS)

I think the young widows, and also possibly some slaves (cf. 1 Tim. 6:1-2), were
surrogate speakers for the false teachers (cf. Gordon Fee's First and Second Timothy and
Titus in the New International Biblical Commentary Vol. 13).

▣ "deprived of the truth" Both of these last phrases are
PERFECT PASSIVE PARTICIPLES, implying a settled state of mind and heart
brought about by an outside agent, probably the evil one. He is the father not only of lies, but
also of religious speculation and theological elitism.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SATAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: TRUTH IN JOHN'S WRITINGS

SPECIAL TOPIC: TRUTH IN PAUL'S WRITINGS

▣

NASB
"who suppose that godliness is a means of gain"

NKJV
"who suppose that godliness is a means of gain"

NRSV
"imagining that godliness is a means of gain"

TEV
"They think that religion is a way to become rich"

NJB
"imagine that religion is a way of making a profit"

Peshitta
"who think worshipping God is for worldly gain"

This seems to involve one of two things:

- The false teachers taught a theology of success, privilege, and possessions.

- They charged for their teaching (cf. Titus 1:11; 2 Pet. 2:3).

- Number 2 is probably more likely.

The King James Version adds a phrase at the end of 1 Tim. 6:5, "from
such withdraw thyself," but this only occurs in the Corrector of the fifth century Greek
uncial manuscript D. It does not occur in the more ancient uncial manuscripts
א, A, D*, F, or G. The UBS4
gives the shorter text an "A" rating (certain).

For "godliness" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GODLINESS

verses.zh: 然而，敬虔加上知足的心便是大利了；
verses.en: Now godliness combined with contentment brings great profit.
verses.commentary:
6:6 "when accompanied by contentment" This word basically involves not prideful
self-sufficiency, but the Holy Spirit-encouraged sufficiency that comes not from circumstance
or personal resources, but dependence on God in Christ (cf. Phil. 4:11-13).

verses.zh: 因为我们没有带甚么到世上来，也不能带甚么去。
verses.en: For we have brought nothing into this world and so[NOTE:1] we cannot take a single thing out either.
notes: The Greek conjunction ὅτι usually means “because,” but here it takes the sense “so that” (see BDAG 732 s.v. 5.c). This unusual sense led to textual variation as scribes attempted to correct what appeared to be an error: D* along with a few versional and patristic witnesses read ἀληθὲς ὅτι (“it is true that”), and א2 D1 Ψ 1175 1241 1505 M al sy read δῆλον ὅτι (“it is clear that”). Thus the simple conjunction is preferred on internal as well as external grounds, supported by א* A F G 048 33 81 1739 1881.
verses.commentary:
6:7 "For we have brought nothing into the world" This may be an allusion to several
OT passages (cf. Job 1:21; Ps. 49:17; Eccl. 5:15). It gives a rationale for the statement in 1 Tim. 6:6.
Verses 6 and 8 are similar to statements found in the Greek Stoic philosophers. Paul was familiar
with these moralists. Many of his lists of sins and virtues are also similar to these Greek writers.

Textual options:

- The KJV adds "and it is certain" for "because" of "for." This addition appears in MSS
אi2 and D2,
as well as some Old Latin, Vulgate, and Syrian versions.

- MS D and some Old Latin, Vulgate, and Syriac versions have "true" before "because."

- The UBS4 gives the shorter text an "A" rating (certain).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KOSMOS

SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM

verses.zh: 只要有衣有食，就当知足。
verses.en: But if we have food and shelter, we will be satisfied with that.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “with these.”
verses.commentary:
6:8 Believers need to be content with God's provision of daily needs
(cf. Prov. 30:8; Matt. 6:11). Paul's use of the word "gain" in 1 Tim. 6:5 caused him to
elaborate on the false teachers' greed (cf. 1 Tim. 6:6-10 and 17-19).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

verses.zh: 但那些想要发财的人，就陷在迷惑、落在网罗和许多无知有害的私欲里，叫人沉在败坏和灭亡中。
verses.en: Those who long to be rich, however, stumble into temptation and a trap and many senseless and harmful desires that plunge people into ruin and destruction.
verses.commentary:
6:9 "But those who want to get rich fall into temptation" Believers bring many
things on themselves because of greed for earthly things, power, and popularity
(cf. Prov. 23:4; 28:20; Matt. 6:19-34).

"Temptation" is the Greek term peirasmos, which means "to test
with a view toward destruction."

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK TERMS FOR TESTING AND THEIR CONNOTATIONS

▣ "and a snare" There are three textual variants.

- snare - MSS א, A, D2, H

- snares - minuscules 33, 1175, and the Peshitta and Coptic versions

- snare of the devil - MSS D*, F, G, and the Old Latin version

The UBS4 gives option #1 an "A" rating (certain).

▣ "ruin and destruction" This concept is used several times in the NT
(cf. Matt. 7:13; Rom. 9:22; Phil. 1:28; 3:19; 2 Thess. 2:3; 2 Pet. 2:1; 3:7; Rev. 17:8-11).
It is imagery for the violent ceasing of physical life. This term does not relate to the
theological concept of annihilation (see Edward Fudge, The Fire That Consumes for a
cogent argument for the annihilation of the unbelieving wicked; also a YouTube video
YouTube One Hour Lecture),
which asserts that the spiritually lost do not suffer permanent separation, but at some
point in time the loss of existence (i.e., limited immortality). Annihilationalists would
interpret this literally. This is asserted to be more "humane" of God than an eternal hell.
However, the same term (aiōnion) that describes an eternal heaven in Matt. 25:46
is also used to describe an eternal hell. I have benefitted from watching a YouTube video by
Steve Gregg called, "Hell—Three Christian Views."
YouTube Lecture
- 1:34:57

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL

verses.zh: 贪财是万恶之根。有人贪恋钱财，就被引诱离了真道，用许多愁苦把自己刺透了。
verses.en: For the love of money is the root[NOTE:1] of all evils.[NOTE:2] Some people in reaching for it have strayed from the faith and stabbed themselves with many pains.
notes: This could be taken to mean “a root,” but the phrase “of all evils” clearly makes it definite. This seems to be not entirely true to life (some evils are unrelated to love of money), but it should be read as a case of hyperbole (exaggeration to make a point more strongly).

Many translations render this “of all kinds of evil,” especially to allow for the translation “a root” along with it. But there is no parallel for taking a construction like this to mean “all kinds of” or “every kind of.” The normal sense is “all evils.”
verses.commentary:
6:10 "For the love of money is a root of all sorts of evil" This may have been a well-known
proverb. Money is not the problem; it is the "love" of money that is the problem! The Greek does not
have the DEFINITE ARTICLE with "root" which means it is one of many problems
(cf. 2 Tim. 2:25-26; 3:2-5,7-9). Money is a tool, not a goal. It can become a god (mammon, cf. Matt. 6:24;
Luke 16:9-13).

The NASB translation, like the NKJV and NRSV, tries to soften the Greek
(lit. "for a root of all evils") hyperbole by adding "sorts" (NKJV, NRSV, "kinds of"). Money is not the
only temptation (cf. Col. 3:5), but it is a significant one (cf. 1 Tim. 3:3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

▣ "some by longing for it have wandered away from the faith" Does "faith" here
speak of salvation or godly living? In this context the false teachers have left the faith and are
trying to influence others (cf. Mark 13:22). Greed and financial exploitation (along with sexual
exploitation, as well as claiming special knowledge or insight) is a recurrent characteristic of
false teachers. If money becomes ultimate, it becomes a god. "Mammon" in Matt. 6:24 is capitalized
in NASB because it is assumed to reflect the title of a money god from Syria. Love of money can
become idolatrous. It can cause disastrous results in this life and in the next (cf. 1 Tim. 4:1; 5:8;
2 Tim. 2:25-26; Titus 1:16).

It is hard to discern the difference between a lost false teacher and a duped believer.
Often they look, think, and act alike. Only God knows the heart. He will make the final decision. Jesus'
words in Matthew 7 ("by their fruits you shall know them") and Matthew 13 (the parable of the soils) are very
troubling to our cherished systematic theologies.

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY (APHISTĒMI)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FAITH

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE

verses.zh: 但你这属　神的人要逃避这些事，追求公义、敬虔、信心、爱心、忍耐、温柔。
verses.en: But you, as a person dedicated to God,[NOTE:1] keep away from all that.[NOTE:2] Instead pursue righteousness, godliness, faithfulness, love, endurance, and gentleness.
notes: Grk “O man of God.”
Grk “flee these things.”
verses.commentary:
6:11 "But flee from these things" Timothy is commanded (PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE,
cf. 2 Tim. 2:22) to flee from the things discussed in 1 Tim. 6:3-10 (i.e., endless controversies and/or love of money).
This is in contrast to the things he was to preach and teach (cf. 1 Tim. 6:2b), which are listed in 1 Tim. 5:1-6:2a.
Christianity involves initial and continuing choices!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣

NASB. NRSV, TEV
"you man of God"

NKJV, Peshitta
"O man of God"

NJB
"as someone dedicated to God"

This was an honorific title from the OT which was used of Moses
(i.e., Deut. 33:1; Josh. 14:6), Elijah, Elisha, Samuel, David, and unnamed prophets
(i.e., 1 Sam. 2:27; 1 Kgs. 12:22; 13:1). In 2 Tim. 3:16,17 it is used for all believers equipped
by the word of God. The false teachers are not men of God nor are they equipped by the
Word of God.

▣ "pursue" This is another PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE, an
ongoing command. The first ("flee") is negative, the second, IMPERATIVE ("pursue")
is positive. Both are crucial for sound teaching and personal righteousness.

▣ "righteousness" This must refer to holy living (cf. James 3:13-18), not to
imputed (forensic) righteousness as in Romans 4. Romans 1-8 (a doctrinal summary) speaks
of our position in Christ (i.e., justification). The Pastoral Letters (letters against false teaching)
speak of our possessing our possession (i.e., sanctification).

This list of Christlike qualities is exactly opposite of the lifestyles of the
false teachers. By their fruits you shall know them (cf. Matth. 7:15-23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "godliness" This is a recurring theme (cf. 1 Tim. 3:10; 4:7-8; 6:3,5-6;
2 Tim. 3:5). Eternal life has observable characteristics. To know God is to be (desire to be)
like God (cf. Matt. 5:48).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GODLINESS

▣

NASB, NJB
"perseverance"

NKJV, Peshitta
"patience"

NRSV, TEV
"endurance"

The Greek word hupomonē has several possible English
translations. In A Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament, Bauer, Arndt, Gingrich,
and Danker say that this word refers to the enduring of toil and suffering (p. 846). Timothy was to face

- the problems

- those who caused the problems

- those affected by the problems with a steadfast endurance

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE

▣ "gentleness" Not only was Timothy to endure and persevere, but he
was to do so with a faithful, loving, gentle spirit (cf. 1 Tim. 3:3; 2 Tim. 2:25; Titus 3:3;
Gal. 6:1; James 1:21; 3:13,17; 1 Pet. 2:18; 3:4).

verses.zh: 你要为真道打那美好的仗，持定永生。你为此被召，也在许多见证人面前，已经作了那美好的见证。
verses.en: Compete well[NOTE:1] for the faith and lay hold of that eternal life you were called for and made your good confession[NOTE:2] for[NOTE:3] in the presence of many witnesses.
notes: This phrase literally means “compete in the good competition of the faith,” using words that may refer to a race or to a boxing or wrestling match: “run the good race” or “fight the good fight.” The similar phrase in 1 Tim 1:18 uses a military picture and is more literally “war the good warfare.”

At some point in Timothy’s life, he publicly acknowledged Jesus as the resurrected Lord, perhaps either at his baptism or his ordination as a minister of the gospel. With this reminder of the historical moment of his good confession, Timothy is encouraged to remain steadfast in his faith and to finish his life as a minister in the same way it began (see G. W. Knight, Pastoral Epistles [NIGTC], 264-65).
Grk “confessed the good confession.”
verses.commentary:
6:12 "Fight the good fight of faith" This is a PRESENT MIDDLE (deponent)
IMPERATIVE. The cognate VERB and NOUN are
used here to intensify the athletic (cf. 1 Tim. 1:18; Heb. 12:1-3) or military (cf. Eph. 6:10-18)
imagery (Paul also "fought the good fight," cf. 2 Tim. 4:7). We get the English word "agony"
from this imagery.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FAITH

▣ "take hold of the eternal life" This is an AORIST MIDDLE IMPERATIVE
(cf. 1 Tim. 6:19). This is imagery for the winning athlete receiving the trophy or crown. This
shows mankind's need to initially respond (cf. 1 Tim. 6:12b) and continue to respond in faith. The
next phrase shows God's keeping power (cf. 1 Tim. 6:12c). These are both true and valid covenantal
aspects of salvation; they are paradoxical, but true (cf. Phil. 2:12-13)! Eternal life is a way of referring to the consummation
of the gospel hope (i.e. glorification, cf. Rom. 8:30; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HOPE). See full note at 2 Tim. 1:10.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "to which you were called" This emphasis on God's electing and keeping power
(cf. 1 Cor. 1:9) must be combined with our daily faith cooperation. Predestination and perseverance
must be held together as two sides of one coin.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALLED

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION AND THE NEED FOR A THEOLOGICAL BALANCE

▣ "and you made the good confession" This is the Greek word homologeō,
which speaks of a public profession or confession (cf. 1 John 1:9). In this context it seems to refer to Timothy's
baptism as his public profession of faith. Early believers may have repeated the formula "Jesus is Lord"
(cf. Rom. 10:9-13) as their personal and public profession of faith in Jesus. This brief phrase implied
His humanity, Deity, atonement, and exaltation (cf. Phil. 2:6-11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONFESSION/PROFESSION

SPECIAL TOPIC: BAPTISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRIST JESUS AS LORD

▣ "in the presence of many witnesses" This may refer to

- Timothy's ordination (cf. 1 Tim. 5:14; 2 Tim. 1:6)

- his public profession before the local church (cf. Acts 16:1-2)

- more probably, his baptism

verses.zh: 我在叫万物生活的　神面前，并在向本丢•彼拉多作过那美好见证的基督耶稣面前嘱咐你：
verses.en: I charge you[NOTE:1] before God who gives life to all things and Christ Jesus who made his good confession[NOTE:2] before Pontius Pilate,
notes: Grk “I charge.” tc ‡ Most witnesses, some of them significant (א2 A D H 1175 1505 1881 M al lat sy bo), have σοι (soi, “you”) after παραγγέλλω (parangellō, “I charge [you]”), a predictable variant because the personal pronoun is demanded by the sense of the passage (and was added in the translation because of English requirements). Hence, the omission is the harder reading, and the addition of σοι is one of clarification. Further, the shorter reading is found in several significant witnesses, such as א* F G Ψ 6 33 1739. Although the external evidence is evenly balanced, internally the shorter reading is preferred. NA 28 places σοι in brackets, indicating some doubts as to its authenticity.
Grk “testified the good confession.”sn Jesus’ good confession was his affirmative answer to Pilate’s question “Are you the king of the Jews?” (see Matt 27:11, Mark 15:2, Luke 23:3, John 18:33-37).
verses.commentary:
6:13 "I charge you in the presence of God" Verses 13-16 are one sentence in
Greek. As Timothy confessed Jesus publicly (cf. Matt. 10:32-33), now Paul charges him
also in God's presence (cf. 1 Tim. 5:21; 2 Tim. 4:1).

Paul "charges" or commands Timothy often in the Pastoral Letters.
Sometimes these refer to things that Timothy should do (cf. 1 Tim. 1:3,18; 4:11; 5:21; 6:13;
2 Tim. 4:1) and sometimes to what he should tell others (cf. 1 Tim. 5:7,21; 6:17; 2 Tim. 2:14).

The PRONOUN "you" is in the INFINITIVE
"to keep" of 1 Tim. 6:14. Some MSS inserted it after the VERB "I charge" in
1 Tim. 6:13 (MSS אi2,
A, D, H). It is omitted in MSS א*, F, G. UBS4
cannot decide which is original. Obviously, like so many Greek variants, it does not affect the
meaning of the long sentence from verse 13 to verse 16.

▣

NASB, NKJV, REB, TEV, NRSV, NET
"gives life"

Peshitta
"the giver of life"

NJB
"the source of all life"

This is literally "bring forth life (PRESENT ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) to all things." God
is the origin and source of all life (cf. 1 Tim. 1:17; 6:16; 2 Tim. 1:10). There is no life apart from Him. The OT title YHWH, from
the Hebrew VERB "to be" (cf. Exod. 3:14), is a word play on this very concept.
God is the only one who can give and sustain physical and eternal life.

This term has connotations of both

- giving life (cf. 1 Sam. 2:6; 1 Tim. 6:13)

- preserving life (cf. Jdgs. 8:19; 1 Sam. 27:9,11; 1 Kgs. 21:31; Luke 17:33; Acts 7:19)

YHWH does both through Christ.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN, C. and D.

▣ "and of Christ Jesus, who testified the good confession before Pontius
Pilate" Jesus is called the "Faithful witness" (cf. Rev. 1:5; 3:14). The term "before"
(enōpion) can mean

- "front of"

- "in the time of"

Therefore, this could refer to Jesus' entire life of witness or specifically His trials (cf. Matt. 27:2; John 18:33-37).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PONTIUS PILATE

verses.zh: 要守这命令，毫不玷污，无可指责，直到我们的主耶稣基督显现。
verses.en: to obey[NOTE:1] this command[NOTE:2] without fault or failure until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ
notes: The Greek word τηρέω (tēreō, traditionally translated “keep”) in this context connotes preservation of and devotion to an object as well as obedience.
Grk “the command.”sn The command refers to the duties laid upon Timothy for his ministry in Ephesus (1 Tim 1:3-20; 6:2c-5).
verses.commentary:
6:14 "that you keep the commandment without stain or reproach" This may refer to
1 Tim. 6:11 and 12. Timothy was to live in obedience and purity, unlike the false teachers.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GODLINESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLAMELESS, INNOCENT, GUILTLESS, WITHOUT REPROACH

▣ "until the appearing of" In 2 Tim. 1:10 and Titus 2:11 this term
(epiphaneia) is used of Jesus' first coming, but here and in 2 Thess. 2:8;
2 Tim. 4:1,8; Titus 2:13 it is used of His Second Coming. The Second Coming has
always been a strong incentive to live the Christian life.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NT TERMS FOR CHRIST'S RETURN

verses.zh: 到了日期，那可称颂、独有权能的万王之王、万主之主，
verses.en: —whose appearing[NOTE:1] the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords, will reveal at the right time.
notes: Grk “which.” All of 1 Tim 6:15 is a relative clause which refers back to “appearing” in v.14. The phrase “whose appearing” was supplied to clarify this connection.
verses.commentary:
6:15 "which He will bring about at the proper time" This same phrase is used in 1 Tim. 2:6
and Titus 1:3 of Jesus' first coming. The "He" describes God the Father's knowledge and control
over the first and second comings of the Messiah (cf. Matt. 24:36; Acts 1:7). The Jerome Biblical
Commentary (p. 357) suggests that 1 Tim. 6:15-16 are a quote from a Christian hymn
(like 1 Tim. 1:17; 3:16; 2 Tim. 2:11-13).

▣ "He who is the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords"
This prayer is similar to 1 Tim. 1:17. These descriptive phrases initially and contextually refer to God the Father:

- "blessed" (1 Tim. 1:1)

- "only Sovereign" (1 Tim. 1:17; cf. Ecclesiasticus 46:5)

- "Lord of lords" (Deut. 10:17; Ps. 136:3)

The title "King of kings" is parallel to "Lord of lords" and is used of Jesus in
Rev. 17:14; 19:16. It originally referred to the kings of Mesopotamia, but was used by the Jews
during the interbiblical period to refer to YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (NT)

verses.zh: 就是那独一不死、住在人不能靠近的光里，是人未曾看见、也是不能看见的，要将他显明出来。但愿尊贵和永远的权能都归给他。阿们！
verses.en: He alone possesses immortality and lives in unapproachable light, whom no human has ever seen or is able to see. To him be honor and eternal power! Amen.
verses.commentary:
6:16 "who alone possesses immortality" This is the term "death" with the
ALPHA PRIVATIVE (cf. 1 Cor. 15:53-54). This seems to be the basic
meaning of the OT title "YHWH," the ever-living, only-living One (cf. Exod. 3:14-16).
Notice the inference of monotheism (i.e., "who alone possesses")! YHWH is the origin
and source of life and there is no other! There is no life apart from Him. See F. F. Bruce,
Answers to Questions, p. 215.

The ancient Greek philosophers (esp. Plato) assert the pre-existence and
post existence immortality of the spiritual aspect of humans known as the "soul." However,
this verse clearly expresses the biblical truth that only YHWH is "eternal." Only He has immortality.

The mortality of Adam and Eve, after they violated YHWH's command, is seen
by their being removed from the Tree of Life. Eternal life is a gift from God, given to believers in Jesus
Christ (i.e., 1 Cor. 15:53,54; 2 Cor. 5:4). The early church fathers, especially Augustine, were affected
by the Platonic presupposition.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

▣ "and dwells in unapproachable light" The rabbis called the "cloud of glory"
the Shekinah, which is from the Hebrew term "to dwell" (with the implication "to dwell
with permanently," cf. Exod. 24:17; 23:20; see notes online).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

▣ "whom no man has seen or can see" In the OT God's holiness was so awesome
that no sinful human could see God and live (cf. Gen. 16:13; 32:30; Exod. 20:19; 33:18-20;
Jdgs. 6:22-23; 13:22; Isa. 6:5; John 6:46; 1 John 4:12). In the NT believers have seen Him truly
revealed in Jesus (cf. John 1:18; 6:46; 14:8-9) and will see Him personally one day (cf. Matt. 5:8;
Heb. 12:14; Rev. 22:40).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CAN HUMANS SEE GOD AND LIVE?

▣ "to Him be honor and eternal dominion" Paul often breaks into a doxology
of praise to God the Father (cf. 1 Tim. 1:17; Eph. 3:20-21). The Son is the Father's instrument of creation,
revelation, redemption, and judgment. However, the eternal kingdom belongs to the Father
through the Son (cf. Dan. 7:13; 1 Cor. 15:25-28).

▣ "Amen" This is a Hebrew idiom of affirmation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN

verses.zh: 你要嘱咐那些今世富足的人，不要自高，也不要倚靠无定的钱财；只要倚靠那厚赐百物给我们享受的　神。
verses.en: Command those who are rich in this world’s goods[NOTE:1] not to be haughty or to set their hope on riches, which are uncertain,[NOTE:2] but on God who richly provides us with all things for our enjoyment.
notes: Grk “in the present age.”
Grk “in uncertainty.”
verses.commentary:
6:17-19 One wonders if 1 Tim. 6:17-19 were an after thought or if Paul received more information
about the house churches in Ephesus. It is also possible that Paul wrote 1 Tim. 6:17-21 himself,
as he regularly closed his letters with his own handwriting (cf. 2 Thess. 3:17-18).

6:17 "Instruct those who are rich in this present world not to be conceited" As verse 9
warns about an evil desire for money, verse 17 warns those who have money against putting
their faith in it and not in Christ (cf. Matt. 6:19-21; 13:22; 19:23-30; James 1:9-11; 5:1-6).

For "this present world" see

SPECIAL TOPIC: THIS AGE AND THE AGE TO COME

▣ "or to fix their hope on the uncertainty of riches" This is a PERFECT ACTIVE INFINITIVE.
Humans tend to trust in their resources, not God's resources (cf. 1 Tim. 4:10; 5:5). Some of Jesus' strongest
words were directed at the wealthy (cf. Luke 18:18-30).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOPE

- on God - א, F, G

- on (the) God - MSS A, I, P

- on God living - MS D*

- on (the) God (the) living - MS D2

The UBS4 gives option #1 an "A" rating. The descriptive form is taken from 1 Tim. 4:10.

verses.zh: 又要嘱咐他们行善，在好事上富足，甘心施舍，乐意供给（或译：体贴）人，
verses.en: Tell them to do good,[NOTE:1] to be rich in good deeds, to be generous givers, sharing with others.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “to do good” (the continuation of 6:17). Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started at the beginning of v. 18.
Grk “to be generous,” “sharing.”
verses.commentary:
6:18 "Instruct them" Here are Paul's threefold guidelines for those who
have worldly goods.

- continue doing good (cf. 1 Tim. 5:10; 2 Tim. 2:21; 3:17; Titus 3:1,8,14)

- be ready to share

- be generous (cf. 2 Corinthians 8-9)

verses.zh: 为自己积成美好的根基，预备将来，叫他们持定那真正的生命。
verses.en: In this way they will save up[NOTE:1] a treasure for themselves as a firm foundation[NOTE:2] for the future and so lay hold of[NOTE:3] what is truly life.
notes: Grk “saving up” (the continuation of 6:18). Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started at the beginning of v. 19.
Grk “treasuring up a good foundation.”
Grk “that they may lay hold of.”
verses.commentary:
6:19 This verse reminds one of Jesus' Sermon on the Mount, especially chapter 6
(cf. Luke 12:15). It uses two examples:

- storing up true riches

- building a sure and strong foundation (i.e., Matt. 7:24-27)

The wise use of wealth does both! By them believers take hold of true life
(i.e., eternal life, cf. 1 Tim. 6:12).

verses.zh: 提摩太啊，你要保守所托付你的，躲避世俗的虚谈和那敌真道、似是而非的学问。
verses.en: O Timothy, protect what has been entrusted to you. Avoid[NOTE:1] the profane chatter and absurdities[NOTE:2] of so-called “knowledge.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “avoiding.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Or “contradictions.”
Grk “the falsely named knowledge.”
verses.commentary:
6:20-21 These closing verses (also possibly 1 Tim. 6:17-19) may have been hand written
by Paul himself to authenticate the letter (cf. 2 Thess. 3:17-18).

6:20 "guard what has been entrusted to you" The VERB is an
AORIST ACTIVE IMPERATIVE. The term "entrusted" is related to the banking
term for "deposit," which is used three times in the Pastoral Letters for "the gospel"
(cf. 1 Tim. 1:11, see full note at 1 Tim. 1:18) or the body of Christian truth (cf. Acts 6:7; 13:8;
14:22; Gal. 1:23; 3:23; 6:10; Phil. 1:27; Jude 1:3,20). Believers are stewards of the gospel
(cf. 1 Cor. 4:1-2; 2 Tim. 1:12,14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ORTHODOXY OF THE PASTORALS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

▣ "avoiding worldly and empty chatter and the opposing arguments
of what is falsely called knowledge" "Avoiding" is a PRESENT MIDDLE PARTICIPLE
used as an IMPERATIVE. 1 Timothy is a letter primarily about heresy, not
church organization. The guidelines in the book are directly related to the problems caused
by the false teachers, not necessarily universal guidelines for all churches of all times in all places.

▣ "knowledge" The false teachers in the Pastoral Letters are a combination of
"Jewish legalists" and Greek Gnostics (much like those in Colossians and Ephesians). "Knowledge,"
usually secret or specially revealed knowledge, was the claim of these teachers. These false teachers
separated truth from life, justification from sanctification, and turned salvation into a secret, special
knowledge divorced from godliness.

verses.zh: 已经有人自称有这学问，就偏离了真道。愿恩惠常与你们同在！
verses.en: By professing it, some have strayed from the faith.[NOTE:1] Grace be with you all.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “have deviated concerning the faith.”

Most witnesses (א2 D1 Ψ 1175 1241 1505 M al sy bo) conclude this letter with ἀμήν (amēn, “amen”). Such a conclusion is routinely added by scribes to NT books because a few of these books originally had such an ending (cf. Rom 16:27; Gal 6:18; Jude 25). A majority of Greek witnesses have the concluding ἀμήν in every NT book except Acts, James, and 3 John (and even in these books, ἀμήν is found in some witnesses). It is thus a predictable variant. Further, the earliest and best witnesses (א* A D* F G 33 81 1739* 1881 it sa) lack the particle, indicating that the letter concluded with “Grace be with you all.”tn Grk “with you” (but the Greek pronoun indicates the meaning is plural here).
verses.commentary:
6:21

NASB
"which some have professed and thus gone astray from the faith"

NKJV, Peshitta
"by professing it, some have strayed concerning the faith"

NRSV
"by professing it some have missed the mark as regards the faith"

TEV
"for some have claimed to possess it, and as a result

they have lost the way of faith"

NJB
"by adopting this, some have missed the goal of faith"

This same word is used in 1 Tim. 1:6 to describe the false teachers; also
notice 1 Tim. 1:19; 4:1-2; 5:15; 6:10. There are so many strong warnings in this book!

Remember Christianity is

- a person to be welcomed

- doctrine to be believed

- a corresponding life to be lived

If any one of these is de-emphasized or left out, then tremendous problems occur (cf. Matt. 7:21-27).

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY

▣ "Grace be with you" The "you" is PLURAL (MS D). This shows
that the letter, although addressed to an individual (singular "you" in MSS א,
A, F, G), was to be read publicly. Notice Paul prays for them God's grace and true knowledge (cf. 1 Tim. 6:20)!
This same PLURAL ending is in all the Pastoral Letters (cf. 2 Tim. 4:22; Titus 3:15).

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- The subject of false teachers returns (cf. 1 Tim. 1:3-11,19-20; 4:1-5; 6:3-11,17-19). This
entire letter addresses the problems caused by the doctrinal and moral issues raised
by the heretics.

- Verses 1-2 seem out of place, but they probably also relate to the false teachers'
messages about Christian slaves and their new rights and freedoms. The
UBS4 and TEV both see the structure of this section of the book as
Paul encouraging Timothy on how to deal with different groups within the church.

- older men and women (1 Tim. 5:1-2)

- widows (1 Tim. 5:3-11)

- elders (1 Tim. 5:17-25)

- slaves (1 Tim. 6:1-2)

- Surprisingly, 1 Timothy does not end with a series of personal greetings. Paul stayed
longer in Ephesus than in any other city and had tremendous evangelistic results (see Acts 19).
He knew many faithful believers in this city. Why greet only Timothy?

This letter is obviously meant to be read to the assembled church or in the
house churches ("you" is PLURAL in 1 Tim. 6:21). However, it was also

- a personal letter with advice and instructions specifically for Timothy, his Apostolic surrogate

- a letter of recommendation passing on Paul's Apostolic authority to Timothy as his personal representative
